# Investigation Summary

## Symptoms

### GPU training throughput dropped, then stopped
**Description:** Distributed-training throughput on the distributed-training-triage-b200 ParallelCluster fell over the last few days. Compute-node logs pin the last training job (JobId 69) completing at 2026-09-24T19:29:29Z, after which no jobs ran; the B200 GPU hardware was then reclaimed at the 2026-09-27T11:30Z Capacity Block expiry. FSx write bursts (checkpoints) on 2026-09-26/27 then fall to zero, and there are no B200 GPU metrics after the fleet vanished.
**Time:** 2026-09-24T19:29:29Z - 2026-09-27T11:30:00Z

## Findings

### Cause: B200 Capacity Block cr-0013d27d3b3d5dc3b expired; GPU nodes can't launch
**Description:** The p6-b200.48xlarge GPU Capacity Block `cr-0013d27d3b3d5dc3b` was extended on 2026-09-24 (PurchaseCapacityBlockExtension by sureshnt-Isengard), but the extension ended 2026-09-27T11:30Z. After that the reservation went inactive and now returns NotFound. The ParallelCluster `distributed-training-triage-b200` head node's RunInstances calls (launch template `distributed-training-triage-b200-gpu-p6b20048xlarge`) began failing with `Client.InvalidParameterValue: Capacity Reservation cr-0013d27d3b3d5dc3b is not active`, so no B200 GPU compute nodes launch — collapsing training throughput.
**Cascades to:** symptom-throughput-drop

#### Gaps
- **Why no training jobs ran between 2026-09-24 19:29Z and the 09-27 expiry is unconfirmable:** Compute-node logs show the last training job (JobId 69) completed 2026-09-24T19:29:29Z, after which the static B200 nodes stayed powered but idle until the 2026-09-27T11:30Z Capacity Block expiry reclaimed them. Whether no new jobs were submitted (benign: the benchmark's queued jobs 30-69 finished and nothing new was queued) or the scheduler stopped placing work cannot be determined, because the head node's clustermgtd/slurmctld CloudWatch log streams stopped shipping on 2026-08-31 and hold no data for the incident window. This is itself an observability gap worth fixing alongside the capacity-expiry alerting.
- **Head-node scheduler logs unavailable for the incident window:** The head node's clustermgtd, slurmctld, and system-messages CloudWatch streams stopped shipping on 2026-08-31 (clustermgtd last event ~Aug 31 14:29Z, slurmctld ~Aug 27), roughly a month before the incident. As a result the 'Capacity Reservation cr-0013d27d3b3d5dc3b is not active' RunInstances error is NOT retrievable from CloudWatch Logs for the 2026-09-27 window — it is only visible via CloudTrail (where it was confirmed). The causal chain is fully supported by CloudTrail + compute-node logs + metrics; this gap only affects head-node-side log corroboration and should be fixed (restore the CloudWatch agent on the head node) for future triage.

### Hypothesis: Storage (FSx for Lustre) ruled out as the bottleneck
**Description:** Over 2026-09-14 → 2026-09-28 at 1h granularity, aggregate DataReadBytes ≈ 0.0047 MB/s (~0.002% of the ~234 MB/s SCRATCH_2 ceiling), FileServerDiskThroughputUtilization flat at ~0.02%, and FreeDataStorageCapacity stable at >99% free (~1086 GiB). No throughput saturation, no IOPS ceiling pressure, no scratch fill-up. The only notable event was a short-lived IOPS/metadata burst when ClientConnections rose 1→3 around 2026-09-26 04:00 UTC, subsiding by 2026-09-28 — inconsistent with a sustained multi-day degradation. Caveat: read volume is so low the job may barely read from FSx.

### Hypothesis: Network / security-group changes ruled out as the cause

# Mitigation Summary

## Action
Restore lost GPU compute for ParallelCluster distributed-training-triage-b200 by purchasing a new p6-b200.48xlarge Capacity Block and repointing the GPU launch template at it, then stop hard-coding time-limited reservation IDs.

## Reasoning
The Capacity Block cr-0013d27d3b3d5dc3b (2x p6-b200.48xlarge, us-west-2d) expired 2026-09-27T11:30Z and was reclaimed. The launch template distributed-training-triage-b200-gpu-p6b20048xlarge hard-codes that reservation (v4) and an older expired one (v1), so RunInstances fails with 'Capacity Reservation ... is not active.' Offering cb-08f51ed0da4ac0bde (2x p6-b200.48xlarge, us-west-2d, 24h from 2026-09-30T11:30Z, $4,744.32) is available to restore capacity.

## Execution Plan

### Step 1: Prepare

#### 1.1 Capture the rollback baseline: record LatestVersionNumber (4)…
**Type:** command
```
aws ec2 describe-launch-template-versions --launch-template-name distributed-training-triage-b200-gpu-p6b20048xlarge --versions '$Latest' '$Default' --region us-west-2
```
**Purpose:** Capture the rollback baseline: record LatestVersionNumber (4), DefaultVersionNumber (1), and both versions' CapacityReservationId.
**Advisory:** Persist this output to a file before any change — it is the launch-template rollback baseline.

### Step 2: Pre Validate

#### 2.1 Confirm offering cb-08f51ed0da4ac0bde is still available and capture…
**Type:** command
```
aws ec2 describe-capacity-block-offerings --instance-type p6-b200.48xlarge --instance-count 2 --capacity-duration-hours 24 --start-date-range 2026-09-28T20:00:00Z --end-date-range 2026-10-07T19:00:00Z --region us-west-2
```
**Purpose:** Confirm offering cb-08f51ed0da4ac0bde is still available and capture its id and upfront fee.
**Risks:** Capacity Block offering IDs are short-lived; if cb-08f51ed0da4ac0bde is gone, pick the closest equivalent 2x p6-b200.48xlarge / us-west-2d offering.
**Advisory:** The API caps the end-date range to ~7 days out.

#### 2.2 Re-confirm the launch template references are unchanged from the…
**Type:** command
```
aws ec2 describe-launch-template-versions --launch-template-name distributed-training-triage-b200-gpu-p6b20048xlarge --versions '$Latest' '$Default' --region us-west-2
```
**Purpose:** Re-confirm the launch template references are unchanged from the prepare-phase backup right before modifying.

### Step 3: Apply

#### 3.1 Purchase the new Capacity Block to restore 2x p6-b200.48xlarge; capture…
**Type:** command
```
aws ec2 purchase-capacity-block --capacity-block-offering-id cb-08f51ed0da4ac0bde --instance-platform Linux/UNIX --tag-specifications 'ResourceType=capacity-reservation,Tags=[{Key=cluster,Value=distributed-training-triage-b200}]' --region us-west-2
```
**Purpose:** Purchase the new Capacity Block to restore 2x p6-b200.48xlarge; capture the returned CapacityReservationId (new cr-xxxx).
**Risks:** Non-refundable upfront charge ~$4,744.32 for the 24h block — verify offering id and fee first., Reservation only becomes active at StartDate 2026-09-30T11:30Z; nodes cannot launch before then.
**Advisory:** Block window is 2026-09-30T11:30Z to 2026-10-01T11:30Z (24h); plan a longer block if the job needs more runway.

#### 3.2 Clone version 4 (preserving all GPU settings) and override only…
**Type:** command
```
aws ec2 create-launch-template-version --launch-template-name distributed-training-triage-b200-gpu-p6b20048xlarge --source-version 4 --version-description 'Point GPU compute at new Capacity Block' --launch-template-data '{"CapacityReservationSpecification":{"CapacityReservationTarget":{"CapacityReservationId":"<NEW_CR_ID>"}}}' --region us-west-2
```
**Purpose:** Clone version 4 (preserving all GPU settings) and override only CapacityReservationId to the new reservation; capture the new VersionNumber (expected 5).
**Risks:** Substitute <NEW_CR_ID> with the exact id from the purchase step; a stale id reproduces the launch failure.
**Advisory:** Cloning v4 avoids reintroducing the older expired reservation cr-0884d02f8b1b344e5 referenced by v1.

#### 3.3 Set the new version as default so the Slurm scaler launches GPU nodes…
**Type:** command
```
aws ec2 modify-launch-template --launch-template-name distributed-training-triage-b200-gpu-p6b20048xlarge --default-version <NEW_VERSION> --region us-west-2
```
**Purpose:** Set the new version as default so the Slurm scaler launches GPU nodes against the new reservation.
**Advisory:** If the scaler does not retry on its own after the reservation is active, recycle the fleet from the head node: pcluster update-compute-fleet --status STOP_REQUESTED then START_REQUESTED for cluster distributed-training-triage-b200.

### Step 4: Post Validate

#### 4.1 Confirm the new reservation exists and transitions to active at…
**Type:** command
```
aws ec2 describe-capacity-reservations --capacity-reservation-ids <NEW_CR_ID> --region us-west-2
```
**Purpose:** Confirm the new reservation exists and transitions to active at 2026-09-30T11:30Z with 2x p6-b200.48xlarge available.

#### 4.2 Confirm 2x p6-b200.48xlarge reach running once the reservation is…
**Type:** command
```
aws ec2 describe-instances --filters 'Name=instance-type,Values=p6-b200.48xlarge' 'Name=instance-state-name,Values=pending,running' --region us-west-2
```
**Purpose:** Confirm 2x p6-b200.48xlarge reach running once the reservation is active and the scaler retries.
**Advisory:** If none appear after the reservation is active, check /var/log/parallelcluster/clustermgtd on head node i-01bbde10b04dd4ca8 for the latest RunInstances error.

### Step 5: Rollback

#### 5.1 Revert the default launch template version to the pre-change baseline…
**Type:** command
```
aws ec2 modify-launch-template --launch-template-name distributed-training-triage-b200-gpu-p6b20048xlarge --default-version 4 --region us-west-2
```
**Purpose:** Revert the default launch template version to the pre-change baseline (v4) if the new version causes issues.
**Risks:** Rollback alone will not restore GPU launches — v4 references the expired cr-0013d27d3b3d5dc3b; use only to undo the template change.
**Advisory:** A purchased Capacity Block cannot be cancelled/refunded; the new reservation remains usable for its window.

## Code Change Specification

### Requirements

#### 1. Stop hard-coding a time-limited Capacity Block reservation ID in the ParallelCluster GPU launch template, and add expiry monitoring.
**Description:** The cluster config for distributed-training-triage-b200 pins the GPU compute resource to a literal Capacity Block reservation ID. When the block expires and is reclaimed, the template points at a dead reservation and the Slurm scaler cannot launch GPU nodes. Source the GPU queue's CapacityReservationTarget from a parameter refreshed on each renewal, and add proactive alerting on the reservation's end time (EventBridge scheduled check or CloudWatch alarm) so an upcoming expiry is surfaced with lead time.
**Acceptance Criteria:**
- The config references the GPU Capacity Block via a single parameterized value updated on renewal, with no expired reservation ID in any active launch template version.
- A documented, repeatable procedure (or automation) exists to purchase a replacement block and repoint the GPU compute resource before the current block ends.
- An alert fires ahead of Capacity Block expiry with enough lead time to renew.
- After a renewal, the Slurm scaler launches 2x p6-b200.48xlarge with no 'Capacity Reservation ... is not active' errors.
